name: Indian Logic
description: The course will discuss Indian theories of inference (anumāna): inference for oneself (svārthānumāna) and inference for the sake of others (parārthānumāna). Different types of logic such as Nyāya logic, Buddhist logic (Nāgārjuna-logic and DignāgaLogic), Jaina logic, Vedānta logic, and Cārvāka’s criticism of inference will be studied. A comparative analysis between Indian logic and categorical syllogism will be discussed. The function of Indian logic in symbolic language will be explored and the problems of logic in natural language will also be examined. In addition that, the course also deals with the applications of Indian logic in academic domains as well as in everyday communication.
